messages.content: Who invented the theory of relativity and in which year?

function.name: science_history_get_invention
function.description: Retrieve the inventor and year of invention based on the invention's name. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

want_year.description: Return the year of invention if set to true.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Who invented the theory of relativity and in which year?" We need to answer: Albert Einstein invented the theory of relativity; the special theory was published in 1905 (the paper "On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies" in Annalen der Physik). The general theory was published in 1915. The question likely refers to the theory of relativity as a whole, but we can mention both. The user didn't specify whether they want the year of invention or publication. The question: "Who invented the theory of relativity and in which year?" So answer: Albert Einstein, 1905 (special) and 1915 (general). But maybe they want just one year. The safe answer: Albert Einstein, 1905. But we can mention both. The user might want the year of invention, not publication. The invention year could be considered 1905 for special relativity. For general relativity, 1915. So answer accordingly.

We should also use the function to retrieve the year of invention. The function signature: science_history_get_invention with parameters: invention_name: string, want_year: boolean. We can call it with invention_name: "theory of relativity", want_year: true. That will return the year. But we need to provide the inventor too. The function only returns the year. We can manually provide the inventor. So we can call the function to get the year. Let's do that.
